# @warlock.js/ai-workspace

A workspace is a policy jail around a directory: it decides which paths an agent may read or write and which shell commands may run, then exposes read, write, edit, multi-edit, list, glob, grep, shell (argv by default, opt-in `sh`, background commands), test and todo tools bound to that policy. Importing the package registers `ai.workspace(...)` on the shared `ai` object.

## The 80% path

1. Create a workspace with a root and policy (`use-a-workspace.md`).
2. Hand its tools to an `ai.agent()`.
3. For a coding agent, follow the read → edit → run tests loop until green (`build-loop-agent.md`).

## Conventions and pitfalls

- The policy is the security boundary: keep the root narrow and the shell allowlist explicit; violations throw `WorkspacePolicyError`.
- Paths resolve inside the jail; escaping it via `..` or symlinks is rejected on purpose.
- The local backend runs real processes. Use `createMockBackend` in tests so no disk or shell is touched.
- Shell refusals carry a `reason` and a message that says how to split the command; `interpreter: "sh"` is an explicit opt-in that still checks every command in the line.
- Call `ws.dispose()` when done: it kills background commands (whole process trees).
- Edits fail loudly (`WorkspaceEditError`) when the target text is not found; re-read the file rather than retrying blindly.

# Build a build-loop agent — read → edit → run tests, until green

The point of a workspace is to hand its tools to an agent and let it close the loop itself: read the failing spec, edit the source, run the tests, read the failure, fix again. The failure comes back as tool **data** (a non-zero `exitCode`, the captured `stderr`), not a thrown error — so the model can see what broke and self-correct.

```ts
import "@warlock.js/ai-workspace";
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";

const ws = ai.workspace({
  cwd: "/srv/acme-api",
  denyPaths: [".git/**", ".env*"],
  shell: { allow: ["npm", "node"], inheritEnv: ["PATH"], timeoutMs: 120_000 },
});

const dev = ai.agent({
  model,
  tools: ws.tools.all(), // read/edit/multi_edit/apply_patch/write, list_dir, run_shell, run_tests, grep, glob, todo_write/todo_read
  maxTrips: 25, // give the loop room to iterate
});

await dev.execute("`npm test` fails on the cart-total suite. Make it green.");
```

## Why the loop works: errors as data

A failing test isn't a tool error — it's a normal result with `exitCode !== 0`. `run_tests` (and `run_shell`) return `{ exitCode, stdout, stderr, timedOut, truncated }` as the tool's `data`, so the model reads the failure on the next trip and tries again. The same is true of the policy/edit guards: a jail escape, a denied command, a non-unique edit, or a stale hash all come back as tool-error data the agent can react to, never a thrown run-killer. Give `maxTrips` enough headroom for the read → edit → test cycle to converge.

## Give the test command a path

`run_tests` defaults to `npm test`. It runs through the **same shell policy** as `run_shell`, so the agent can't run it unless:

- the executable basename is allowed — `shell: { allow: ["npm", "node"] }`, and
- the env can find it — `inheritEnv: ["PATH"]` (the workspace never inherits `process.env` wholesale).

Override the base command per agent: `ws.tools.runTests({ command: "vitest run" })`. A `pattern` the model supplies is appended as a filter (e.g. `vitest run cart-total`).

## Least-privilege variants

### A read-only reviewer

A reviewer should never write or run a shell. Pick exactly the read tools, or hand it a `readonly()` projection (which omits the mutating tools _and_ rejects the mutating direct methods):

```ts
const reviewer = ai.agent({
  model,
  tools: ws.tools.pick("readFile", "grep", "glob"),
});
await reviewer.execute("Review src/cart for off-by-one bugs and summarize.");

// Equivalent projection of the same jail:
ai.agent({ model, tools: ws.readonly().tools.all() }); // read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, todo tools
```

### Scope an agent to one package

`scope(subdir)` narrows the jail so a per-package agent can't reach outside it — one sub-agent per package, isolated blast radius:

```ts
const apiDev = ai.agent({ model, tools: ws.scope("packages/api").tools.all() });
const webDev = ai.agent({ model, tools: ws.scope("packages/web").tools.all() });
```

## Scaffold from code, then hand off

You don't have to let the agent do everything. Seed structure (and install deps) with the direct methods, then hand the tools to the agent for the creative part:

```ts
await ws.writeFile("src/routes.ts", ROUTES_BOILERPLATE);
await ws.exec("npm install zod");
await dev.execute("Implement the handlers declared in src/routes.ts.");
```

For a purely mechanical change, skip the LLM entirely: `ws.glob(...)` + a loop of `ws.editFile(...)` under the stale-hash guard.

## Share one workspace across a team

One workspace is one jail and one tree. Pass it to several members of a supervisor, varying only the tool slice each gets — they all read/write the **same** files:

```ts
const ws = ai.workspace({ cwd, shell: { allow: ["npm", "node"], inheritEnv: ["PATH"] } });

ai.supervisor({
  members: [
    ai.agent({ /* executor */ model, tools: ws.tools.all() }),
    ai.agent({ /* reviewer */ model, tools: ws.readonly().tools.all() }),
    ai.agent({ /* tester   */ model, tools: ws.tools.pick("readFile", "runTests") }),
  ],
});
```

# Use a workspace — a policy jail for an agent's filesystem + shell

`ai.workspace(policy)` returns a **workspace**: a bounded place an agent reads, writes, and runs commands. One policy, one shared rule set, two ways to touch it — the agent uses `ws.tools.*`; you use the direct methods. Import the package once for its side effect so the verb is registered on the shared `ai`:

```ts
import "@warlock.js/ai-workspace";
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";

const ws = ai.workspace({
  cwd: "/srv/acme-api",
  denyPaths: [".git/**", ".env*"],
  shell: { allow: ["npm", "node"], inheritEnv: ["PATH"], timeoutMs: 60_000 },
  read: { defaultLines: 2_000 },
  backend: "local", // default; use "mock" for hermetic tests
});
```

## A policy jail, NOT OS isolation

This is least-privilege guardrails for a **trusted** agent — not a sandbox around hostile code. It enforces a `realpath`-resolved `cwd` jail, path allow/deny, a fail-closed shell allow/deny list, timeouts, output caps, and a non-inherited environment. It does **not** contain what an _allowed_ process does once it runs.

Paths are resolved against `cwd` with symlinks collapsed and accepted inside `cwd` or an `allowPaths` root, off `denyPaths`; absolute paths inside the jail, links that stay inside and not-yet-existing paths (for writes) are accepted. To read a folder you do not trust from app code (no links at all, size and entry caps), use `fs.confined(root)` from `@warlock.js/fs` (the `read-a-folder-confined` topic) instead of a workspace.

**Shell mode (`interpreter: "sh"`) is a policy layer (defence in depth), not an OS sandbox.** It parses the line before `/bin/sh` runs it and refuses what it cannot read, but `/bin/sh` differs between systems (bash, dash, busybox ash), an allowed program (`node`, `npm`, `make`, a git hook) can still start anything the OS user can, and a symlink can change between the jail re-check and the write. For an untrusted agent (one that reads untrusted repos, issues, web pages or tool output), run the workspace in a container or microVM with only the project mounted, or at least as a separate unprivileged user, and keep the policy as a second layer. Prefer argv mode (the default) when the agent does not need pipes or redirections.

## The policy surface

| Field                                                                             | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cwd`                                                                             | **Absolute** jail root. Every path resolves against it and must stay inside.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `allowPaths`                                                                      | Extra readable roots outside `cwd`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `denyPaths`                                                                       | Globs (`*`, `**`, `?`) blocked **even inside `cwd`** — e.g. `[".git/**", ".env*"]`. A bare dir name (`"node_modules"`) also blocks its contents.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `shell.allow` / `shell.deny`                                                      | Executable **basenames** matched against every command's argv (after tokenizing — see below). **Deny wins**, case-insensitively. An `allow` list is exhaustive (fail-closed); no `shell` block at all ⇒ nothing may run.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `shell.denyPatterns` / `shell.allowCommand`                                       | Argument rules on every command: string prefix patterns (`"git push --force"`) or RegExps, and a predicate `(argv, ctx) => true \| false \| "why"`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `shell.interpreter`                                                               | `"none"` (default, argv), `"sh"`, `"bash"`, `"powershell"`, `"cmd"` or `"auto"` (opt-in shell syntax, every command checked); `shell.interpreterPath` sets the shell executable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `shell.rules` / `shell.onAsk`                                                     | Ordered `{ match, effect: "allow" \| "ask" \| "deny", reason? }` rules (last match wins, a deny anywhere refuses the line); `onAsk({ command, asks, signal })` returns `{ allow, remember? }`. Refusals: `"approval-required"`, `"approval-denied"`. `ws.shell.classify(line)` lists a line's commands. `remember` takes one pattern or an array and `reason` (≤ 500 chars) reaches the model in the refusal; `ws.shell.remembered()` / `forget(pattern)` list and remove remembered patterns.        |
| `shell.background`                                                                | `{ maxJobs?, timeoutMs? }` — enables background commands. Absent ⇒ refused.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `list.ignore` / `list.maxDepth` / `list.maxEntries`                               | `list_dir` bounds: hidden globs (default `node_modules`, `.git`), depth cap (5), entry cap (500).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `search.skipDirs` / `search.gitignore` / `search.maxFiles` / `search.concurrency` | What `glob` and `grep` walk: folders never entered (default `[".git", "node_modules"]`, matched by name at any depth or by path glob), whether `.gitignore` files are honoured (default `true`), the most files one search looks at before it stops and sets `truncated` + `maxFilesReached` (default 50000), and how many folders are read at once (default 16). `denyPaths` and the jail apply regardless. A pattern whose leading folder is skipped (`node_modules/pkg/*.json`) still searches it. |
| `shell.inheritEnv`                                                                | Opt-in `process.env` keys to pass through (e.g. `["PATH"]`). **Nothing leaks in otherwise** — a command can't find `node`/`npm` without `PATH`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `shell.env`                                                                       | Explicit env vars injected into every spawned process (override inherited on collision).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `shell.timeoutMs` / `shell.maxOutputBytes`                                        | Per-command wall-clock cap (process tree SIGKILLed on expiry) and stdout/stderr byte cap (clipped on a character boundary).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `read.defaultLines` / `read.maxBytes`                                             | Default read window + a ceiling on the UTF-8 bytes of the returned `content` (line numbers included). See [Read windows and the byte ceiling](#read-windows-and-the-byte-ceiling).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `backend`                                                                         | `"local"` (default — real disk) or `"mock"` (in-memory, for tests).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

> **The most common gotcha:** `run_shell` fails to find `node`/`npm` because the env is empty. Add `shell: { allow: ["npm", "node"], inheritEnv: ["PATH"] }`.

## `run_shell`/`exec` run argv, NOT a shell

Commands are tokenized (via `tokenizeCommand`) into an argv and spawned with **no shell semantics** — no pipes, redirection, chaining, backticks, or variable expansion. `npm test && rm -rf /` or `` `curl evil` `` doesn't chain or substitute; it's rejected outright rather than executed piecemeal:

```ts
await ws.exec("npm test"); // OK — ["npm", "test"]
await ws.exec('node -e "console.log(1)"'); // OK — quotes respected, one argv element
await ws.exec("npm test; curl http://evil"); // rejected — unquoted `;` is a metacharacter
```

- **Quoting is respected**; **unquoted** shell metacharacters — `;` `&` `|` `<` `>` `` ` `` `$` `(` `)` and newlines — are rejected as a `WorkspacePolicyError` `type: "denied-command"` before anything spawns. The `shell.allow`/`shell.deny` basename check runs against the tokenized argv's first element, not a raw string prefix, so a disguised leading token can't slip past the gate.
- **On Windows**, the argv is run through a `cmd.exe /d /s /c` wrapper with every element individually quoted (needed because batch shims like `npm.cmd` can't be spawned shell-less); arguments containing `"`, `%`, or newlines are refused there rather than risked (guards the BatBadBut-class argument-smuggling bug class).
- **`run_tests`'s `pattern`** (model-controlled test-name filter) is forwarded as a **single double-quoted argv token** to the runner, not concatenated into the command string — a pattern containing double quotes or newlines is rejected at input validation rather than passed through.
- Shell conveniences (pipes, redirection, `&&` chaining, `$(...)` substitution) don't work in argv mode. The refusal (`reason: "metacharacter"`) names the operator and suggests the split — e.g. "`&&` is not supported in argv mode: run `git add -A`, then `git commit -m "wip"`, as separate commands." — so the model retries correctly.
- **Wrappers are followed**: `env`, `time`, `timeout`, `nice`, `nohup`, `command`, `builtin`, `exec`, `find -exec` — the inner command is checked too. Runners the policy can't see into (`sh -c`, `bash`, `eval`, `source`, `xargs`, `sudo`, `setsid`, …) are refused with `reason: "nested-command"` while deny rules are in force, unless `allow` names them.

## Argument rules and shell mode

```ts
import { workspace, WorkspacePolicyError } from "@warlock.js/ai-workspace";

export async function commitWork(cwd: string) {
  const ws = workspace({
    cwd,
    shell: {
      interpreter: "sh", // opt in: pipes, &&, redirections — every command still checked
      allow: ["git", "npm", "grep"],
      denyPatterns: ["git push --force", /^git reset --hard\b/],
      allowCommand: (argv) => (argv[0] === "git" && argv[1] === "push" ? "CI pushes." : true),
      inheritEnv: ["PATH"],
      timeoutMs: 120_000,
    },
  });

  try {
    await ws.exec("git add -A && git commit -m 'wip'");
    return await ws.exec("npm test 2>&1 | grep -i fail > logs/failures.txt");
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof WorkspacePolicyError && error.type === "denied-command") {
      console.warn(error.reason, error.message); // e.g. "denied-pattern", "path-escape"
    }

    throw error;
  }
}
```

- Shell mode parses the line and checks every simple command — inside `;`, `&&`, `||`, pipes, `( )`, `$( )`, backticks, here-documents and `NAME=value cmd` prefixes. Redirection targets and `cd` directories must be literal paths inside the jail (`/dev/null` is fine), re-checked with symlinks resolved.
- It refuses what it can't parse with confidence (`reason: "unsupported-syntax"`): compound commands, arithmetic, brace expansion, unusual `${…}` forms, bash-only redirections, a command name decided at run time, `&` in a line (use `background: true`), assignments to `IFS`/`PS4`/`CDPATH`/`BASH_ENV`…; it drops shell start-up variables (`ENV`, `BASH_ENV`, `SHELLOPTS`, `BASH_FUNC_*`, …) from the environment.
- Bash on Windows reads an unquoted backslash as an escape: a line like `cd ab\x\y` is refused (`"unsupported-syntax"`) with the forward-slash form (`ab/x/y`) in the message, and `run_shell`'s description says to write paths with forward slashes. Quoted paths and `a\ b` pass; Linux and macOS are unchanged.
- `reason` values: `"metacharacter"`, `"unbalanced-quotes"`, `"denied-executable"`, `"not-allowed"`, `"denied-pattern"`, `"nested-command"`, `"unsupported-syntax"`, `"path-escape"`. `checkShellCommand(policy, line)` returns the verdict without running anything; `classifyShellCommand(line, policy?)` returns `{ commands, opaque? }` with the same parser a host approval gate can reuse; `resolveShell(policy.shell)` reports which interpreter and executable `"auto"` (or a named interpreter) resolves to on this host, plus the PowerShell `edition` (`"desktop"` = Windows PowerShell 5.1, `"core"` = 7+) and `version`; the 5.1 dialect (`"powershell5"`) refuses `&&` / `||`, and on Windows `"auto"` prefers `pwsh`, then Git Bash, then 5.1, then `cmd`. The `PowerShellEdition` type is exported.
- Pair shell mode with an exhaustive `allow`: `deny` alone is a best-effort filter.

## Two callers, one jail

### Agent-facing — `ws.tools.*`

Each tool is a `ToolContract` (with a JSON Schema of its input) ready for `ai.agent({ tools })`. The LLM-visible tool names are `read_file`, `edit_file`, `multi_edit`, `apply_patch`, `write_file`, `list_dir`, `run_shell`, `shell_output`, `shell_kill`, `run_tests`, `grep`, `glob`, `todo_write`, `todo_read` — `shell_output` / `shell_kill` only in `all()` when `shell.background` is set.

```ts
ws.tools.all(); // every tool, canonical order
ws.tools.pick("readFile", "grep", "glob"); // a least-privilege subset
ws.tools.readFile({ name: "open" }); // one tool, optionally renamed
ws.tools.runTests({ command: "vitest run" }); // override the test base command
```

### Human-facing — direct methods

The same policy seam, callable from code (no LLM):

```ts
const { content, hash, totalLines, endLine, truncated, bytesCapped } = await ws.readFile(
  "src/index.ts",
  { offset: 1, limit: 200 },
);
await ws.writeFile("src/new.ts", "export const x = 1;\n");
await ws.editFile({ path: "src/index.ts", oldString: "old", newString: "new", expectHash: hash });
const { exitCode, stdout, stderr, timedOut, cancelled, truncated } = await ws.exec("npm test");
const { matches } = await ws.grep("TODO", { glob: "src/**/*.ts", ignoreCase: true });
const paths = await ws.glob("src/models/**/*.ts");
await ws.exists("package.json");
await ws.mkdir("src/generated");
await ws.remove("dist");
```

## The coding-agent tool belt

```ts
import { workspace } from "@warlock.js/ai-workspace";

export async function devLoop(cwd: string) {
  const ws = workspace({
    cwd,
    list: { maxEntries: 300 },
    shell: { allow: ["npm", "node"], inheritEnv: ["PATH"], background: { maxJobs: 2 } },
  });

  try {
    const { entries } = await ws.listDir("src", { depth: 2 }); // bounded, jailed, node_modules/.git hidden
    console.info(entries.map((entry) => `${entry.type} ${entry.path}`));

    const { hash } = await ws.readFile("src/cart.ts");
    await ws.multiEdit({
      path: "src/cart.ts",
      expectHash: hash,
      edits: [
        { oldString: "let total = 0;", newString: "let total = 0n;" },
        { oldString: "total += price;", newString: "total += BigInt(price);" },
      ], // all apply, or none (WorkspaceEditError.editIndex names the failing one)
    });

    const server = await ws.startShell("npm run dev"); // run_shell({ command, background: true })
    const { stdout, cursor } = await ws.shellOutput(server.id, { waitMs: 5_000 });
    console.info(stdout, cursor); // pass `since: cursor` to read only what comes next
    await ws.shellKill(server.id); // kills the whole process tree

    ws.writeTodos([{ content: "Fix the rounding bug", status: "completed" }]); // todo_write
    return ws.readTodos().counts; // todo_read
  } finally {
    await ws.dispose(); // kills every background command; the workspace refuses new commands
  }
}
```

- Result shapes when output is cut or spilled (`output.spillDir`): every result that spilled carries a flat `spilledTo?: string[]` (absolute paths) beside `truncated` and `truncation`, and its text ends with the marker line naming the file.
  - `run_shell` → `{ exitCode, stdout, stderr, truncated, timedOut, cancelled, truncation?: { stdout?, stderr? }, spilledTo? }`; one path per spilled stream.
  - `shell_output` → the fields above under Background, plus `truncation?: { stdout?, stderr? }` and `spilledTo?`.
  - `read_file` → `{ content, ..., truncated, bytesCapped, truncation?, spilledTo? }`; spills only when `read.maxBytes` cut the window.
  - `grep` takes `{ pattern, glob?, path?, ignoreCase? }` — `path` is a workspace-relative folder or file to search under (jail/deny-checked; `glob` still matches workspace-relative paths); files are read 16 at a time and binary files (NUL in the first 8000 characters) are skipped → `{ matches, total, truncated?, truncation?, spilledTo? }`; `glob` → `{ paths, truncated?, truncation?, spilledTo?, maxFilesReached? }`. Both start at the pattern's static folder prefix (`src/api/**/*.ts` reads only `src/api`), never enter `node_modules`, `.git`, `denyPaths` folders or gitignored paths (see `search.*`), and take an optional `signal` that stops the walk.
  - `truncation` is `{ shown: { lines }, total: { lines, bytes }, path? }`; without `spillDir` there is no `path` and no `spilledTo`.
- `list_dir({ path?, depth?, ignore? })` → `{ path, entries: [{ path, type, size?, depth }], truncated }`; `denyPaths` always hidden, `list.ignore` (default `node_modules`, `.git`) hidden from listings, symlinks reported but never followed.
- `apply_patch({ patch, dryRun? })` → `{ files: [{ path, action, oldPath?, hunks, hash? }], dryRun }`; a unified diff that modifies, creates, deletes and renames files, all or none; paths jailed, hunks matched by context, line endings kept, binary files refused (`binary-file`); `dryRun` checks only. Not in `readonly()`.
- `multi_edit({ path, edits, expectHash? })` → `{ path, edits, replacements, hash }`; same uniqueness rules as `edit_file`, at most 100 edits.
- Background: `shell_output({ id, since?, waitMs?, until? })` (`until: "exit"` waits for the job to stop, `waitMs` up to 600000, instead of returning at the next output; default `"output"`, max 30000) → `{ stdout, stderr, cursor, droppedBytes, truncated, status, exitCode }`; only the newest `shell.maxOutputBytes` per command are kept. States `"running"`, `"exited"`, `"killed"`, `"timed-out"`. Unknown id → `WorkspaceJobError`. Background commands outlive the agent run; `dispose()` (or process exit) kills them. Only processes the workspace spawned are ever signalled.
- Todos: one in-memory list per workspace, shared with `readonly()` / `scope()`; `todo_write` replaces the whole list (≤ 100 items, status `pending` / `in_progress` / `completed`).
- `run_shell`'s model-supplied `timeoutMs` can only lower `shell.timeoutMs`.

## `grep` is ReDoS-bounded

The model supplies `pattern` freely, so `grep` treats it as untrusted input before compiling it into a `RegExp`: patterns over 200 characters and patterns matching a nested-quantifier shape (`(x+)+`, `(x*)*`, `(x+)*`, `(x*)+`-style groups — the classic catastrophic-backtracking shape) are rejected up front as a `WorkspacePolicyError` `type: "unsafe-pattern"`, before any regex is compiled. Any scanned line longer than 2000 characters is skipped (not tested), bounding the worst-case backtracking cost of any single call regardless of pattern shape.

## Read windows and the byte ceiling

`readFile()` and the `read_file` tool return the same result for the same arguments: a `cat -n` numbered window plus `{ startLine, endLine, totalLines, totalBytes, truncated, bytesCapped, hash }`.

- The window starts at `offset` (`startLine` on the tool) and holds at most `limit` lines (default `read.defaultLines`, else 2000).
- `read.maxBytes` caps the UTF-8 bytes of the returned `content` itself — line-number prefixes and newlines count. Whole lines are kept while they fit; the first line that doesn't is cut on a **character boundary** (never mid-character), so a single very long line still comes back bounded. `bytesCapped` is `true` whenever the cap cut anything, and `endLine` is the last line included, possibly partially.
- `truncated` is `true` when anything after `content` was withheld — later lines (by `limit`, the default window or the cap) or the tail of `endLine`.
- `hash` is always the SHA-256 of the **whole file**, not the window, so it is a valid `expectHash` whatever was returned. `totalBytes` is the whole file's size.
- No `maxBytes` ⇒ no byte cap (only the line window applies).

```ts
const ws = ai.workspace({ cwd, read: { maxBytes: 64_000, defaultLines: 400 } });
const page = await ws.readFile("dist/bundle.js");
if (page.bytesCapped) console.warn(`Only part of line ${page.endLine} fit in the read budget.`);
```

## Cancelling a command

`exec()` accepts a per-call `signal`; `run_shell` and `run_tests` pass the agent run's signal (the dispatch `ctx.signal`) automatically, so cancelling the agent run stops the command it is waiting on.

- Already aborted ⇒ the command is **not started** (`exitCode: 130`).
- Aborted mid-run ⇒ the whole process tree is SIGKILLed, as on a timeout.
- A killed command (timeout, abort, `shell_kill`, `dispose()`) settles within about a second of the kill even when a process outside the killed tree still holds its output pipes open: it returns what was captured so far with `timedOut` / `cancelled` set.
- Either way the result says `cancelled: true` — it resolves, it doesn't throw — and `cancelled` and `timedOut` are never both `true`. Branch on those flags, not on the exit code.
- The signal belongs to that one call; the workspace never stores it, so one workspace can serve many runs. The abort listener is removed once the command settles.

```ts
const controller = new AbortController();
const pending = ws.exec("npm test", { signal: controller.signal, timeoutMs: 120_000 });
controller.abort();
const { cancelled } = await pending; // true
```

A custom `WorkspaceBackend` receives the signal as `exec(command, { signal })` and should follow the same rules, reporting `cancelled: true` in its result.

## Read-before-edit (the stale-hash guard)

`readFile` returns a SHA-256 `hash` of the full file. Pass it to `editFile`'s `expectHash`; if the file changed since you read it, the edit is rejected as stale so you re-read before clobbering. `editFile` also requires the `oldString` to be **found uniquely** (see "Finding the text to edit") — pass `replaceAll: true` to replace every occurrence, or include more surrounding context to disambiguate.

Writes, edits and removes of the same path run one after another, even when the agent dispatches tool calls concurrently: of two edits pinned to the same `expectHash`, the second is rejected as stale instead of silently overwriting the first. `read.maxBytes` bounds what a read returns, not memory — the whole file is still read and hashed.

## Finding the text to edit — `edit.matching`

By default an edit looks for `oldString` in tiers and uses the first tier that finds it: the exact text, then the text with line endings normalised (an LF `oldString` finds CRLF lines), then with look-alike punctuation folded (curly quotes, en/em dashes and non-breaking spaces match their plain forms), then line by line ignoring trailing whitespace. A result found by one of the last two tiers reports `matchTier: "unicode"` or `"whitespace"`; an exact find leaves it out. A loose find must be unique: with two candidates the edit fails with `not-unique` and writes nothing, even with `replaceAll`. Replacement text takes the file's dominant line ending, so a CRLF file stays CRLF.

```ts
ai.workspace({
  cwd,
  edit: { matching: "tiered", missHintLines: 12, lineEndings: "preserve" },
});
```

- `matching: "exact"` accepts only the text byte for byte.
- `lineEndings: "lf" | "crlf"` forces the ending of replacement text.
- When the text is not found, the `WorkspaceEditError` (`type: "not-found"`) carries a `hint`: the closest file text (at most `missHintLines` lines, 12 by default, each at most 200 characters; `0` turns it off, and it never exceeds `read.maxBytes`) or a note that `newString` is already present. A file the jail refuses never gets a hint.

## Diagnostics after an edit — `hooks.afterEdit`

```ts
ai.workspace({
  cwd,
  hooks: {
    afterEdit: async ({ paths, tool }) => await typecheck(paths), // returns text or nothing
    afterEditMaxChars: 4_000,
    afterEditTimeoutMs: 10_000,
  },
});
```

After `write_file`, `edit_file`, `multi_edit` or `apply_patch` writes files, the hook runs once per call with the written paths (not on a patch `dryRun`, not for deleted files). Text it returns comes back on the result as `diagnostics`, between `[diagnostics]` and `[/diagnostics]` lines; output over `afterEditMaxChars` is cut with a marker. A hook that throws or does not answer within `afterEditTimeoutMs` yields `diagnostics unavailable` and never fails the edit.

## Live shell output — `hooks.onShellOutput`

```ts
workspace({
  cwd,
  shell: { allow: ["npm"], env: { API_KEY: process.env.API_KEY! } },
  hooks: {
    onShellOutput: ({ command, stream, chunk, jobId, callId }) => ui.append(chunk),
    redactShellOutput: (text) => text.replace(/sk-[a-z0-9]+/g, "[redacted]"),
  },
});
```

`run_shell` returns its output when the command ends; `onShellOutput` (event type `WorkspaceShellOutputEvent`) lets a host that shows the session to a person see it while the command runs. It fires for foreground commands and for background jobs (`jobId` is set; it keeps firing after `run_shell` has returned). Text is decoded, in order per stream, delivered at most about 20 times a second (faster output is merged), and never changes the result the agent gets (truncation and spilling are as before). A hook that throws is ignored. Pass `callId` to `ws.exec(command, { callId })` (or `ws.startShell(command, { callId })` for a background job, whose events then carry both `jobId` and `callId`) to have it echoed on the command's events. The `run_shell` tool does this itself with the model's tool-call id (`ctx.callId`), so two concurrent commands with the same text stay distinguishable. A backend that cannot stream delivers the whole capture once, when the command ends.

The workspace redacts nothing in results, so live text is raw unless you mask it. Redaction needs a secret in one piece but a process writes in arbitrary pieces, so output is buffered to line boundaries first and then redacted: a secret split across two reads is whole by the time `redactShellOutput(text)` sees it. The unfinished last line is held until its newline arrives or the command ends (a line over 16 KB is cut, keeping its last 512 characters back). Values in `shell.env` of eight or more characters are masked as `[redacted]` before `redactShellOutput` runs. If the redactor throws, that text is dropped, never delivered unmasked. A secret that contains a newline cannot be matched this way.

## Oversized output — `output`

```ts
ai.workspace({
  cwd,
  output: {
    spillDir: ".warlock/spill",
    maxLines: 2_000,
    maxBytes: 51_200,
    retentionMs: 604_800_000,
  },
});
```

With `output.spillDir` set, output too large to return whole (`run_shell`, `shell_output`, `grep`, `glob`, and `read_file` when `read.maxBytes` cut the window) is saved in full to `spill-<time>-<random>-<label>.txt` there. The result keeps the start and end (`keep: "head+tail"`, the default for shell output; `"head"` for the rest, or set `keep` yourself) and carries a marker such as `[showing lines 1-25 and 99976-100000 of 100000; full output saved to FILE]`. The boolean `truncated` stays; `truncation` adds `{ shown: { lines }, total: { lines, bytes }, path? }` (per stream, `truncation.stdout` / `truncation.stderr`, for commands). `read_file` may open the spill directory even when it is outside the jail, so the model can page through the file with `startLine` / `limit`; nothing else outside the jail opens, and writes never reach it. Files older than `retentionMs` (7 days by default) are removed when a workspace is created, when a new file is written and on `dispose()`; `retentionMs: 0` removes the files this workspace wrote on `dispose()`. Only files named like spill files are ever removed. Without `spillDir`, output is cut at `shell.maxOutputBytes` / `read.maxBytes` as before, and `run_shell` results still report the sizes in `truncation`.

## Errors flow as data, not throws

Policy and edit failures are typed errors extending the `@warlock.js/ai` `AIError` base. Inside a tool the `tool()` wrapper catches them and surfaces them in `{ error }`, so the agent reads the failure and self-corrects. Branch on `.type`:

```ts
import { WorkspacePolicyError, WorkspaceEditError } from "@warlock.js/ai-workspace";

try {
  await ws.exec("rm -rf /");
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof WorkspacePolicyError && error.type === "denied-command") {
    console.warn(`Blocked: ${error.command}`);
  }
}
```

- `WorkspacePolicyError.type`: `"path-escape"` (jail escape / deny glob) | `"denied-command"` (the shell policy refused the line — `reason` says why) | `"unsafe-pattern"` (`grep` pattern too long or nested-quantifier ReDoS shape).
- `WorkspaceEditError.type`: `"not-found"` | `"not-unique"` | `"stale-hash"` | `"patch-invalid"` | `"hunk-failed"` | `"binary-file"` | `"file-exists"` | `"file-missing"` (+ `editIndex` for `multiEdit`, `hunkIndex` for `applyPatch`).
- `WorkspaceJobError.type`: `"not-found"` (unknown background command id).

## Composition — `readonly()` and `scope()`

```ts
const ro = ws.readonly(); // vends only read/grep/glob; mutating direct methods reject
const api = ws.scope("packages/api"); // a sub-jailed workspace rooted at the subdir
```

`readonly()` is the least-privilege reviewer projection — `tools.all()` on it returns `read_file`, `list_dir`, `grep`, `glob` and the todo tools only, and `writeFile` / `editFile` / `multiEdit` / `applyPatch` / `exec` / `startShell` / `shellKill` / `mkdir` / `remove` throw a `WorkspacePolicyError`. Projections share the workspace's background commands and todo list. `scope(subdir)` narrows `cwd` to `join(cwd, subdir)` (same sub-policies, same backend), so a per-package agent gets a tighter blast radius.

## Hermetic tests with the mock backend

`backend: "mock"` swaps the local disk for an in-memory `Map` + scripted `exec` — same policy, same tool/method surface, no filesystem:

```ts
const ws = ai.workspace({ cwd: "/srv/app", backend: "mock", shell: { allow: ["npm"] } });
// (Seed files / scripted commands via createMockBackend when constructing a backend directly.)
```

## See also

- The `build-loop-agent` topic — wiring these tools into a read → edit → test agent loop.
- The `run-ai-agent` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — running the agent that consumes `ws.tools.all()`.
- The `define-ai-tool` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — the `tool()` / `ToolContract` seam every workspace tool is built on.

## Complete bounded-read and cancellation example

```ts
import { workspace } from "@warlock.js/ai-workspace";

export async function inspectWorkspace(cwd: string) {
  const ws = workspace({
    cwd,
    read: { maxBytes: 64_000, defaultLines: 400 },
    shell: { allow: ["node"], inheritEnv: ["PATH"] },
  });
  const page = await ws.readFile("package.json");
  console.info(page.bytesCapped, page.endLine, page.hash);

  const controller = new AbortController();
  controller.abort();
  const result = await ws.exec('node -e "console.log(1)"', { signal: controller.signal });
  if (result.cancelled) console.info("Command cancelled before it started");
  return page;
}
```

The caller supplies an absolute existing workspace root. The already-aborted
signal demonstrates the no-spawn path; a later abort also kills a running
command's process tree. The byte ceiling limits returned content, while the
hash still describes the whole file.
